Category.reason: Confirmed. The similarity-network-fusion model takes three co-equal input modalities, each turned into its own similarity matrix before fusion: cognitive/neuropsychological scores (ADAS, RAVLT, mPACCdigit, mPACCtrailsB, LDELTOTAL, TRABSCOR, FAQ; C5), genetics (APOE status and polygenic hazard score; C3) and seven structural MRI volumes (ventricles, hippocampus, whole brain, entorhinal, fusiform, middle temporal, ICV; C1). The paper's own statement of its contribution names all three. The registry keeps only C3, which is the smallest input (two genetic variables; blood-transcriptome GSVA and CSF are used afterwards to characterise the clusters), and leaves out two primary input domains, MRI and neuropsych. Under the rule, a missing primary data domain is an error, not an omitted secondary domain. PET (AV45, FDG) and CSF only characterise the clusters and add nothing beyond C1/C3.
Category.quote: This study presents a novel application of SNF to integrate cognitive, genetic, and structural MRI data, enabling the simultaneous identification of disease subtypes in AD.
